card.name: Health news article openers and quote starts
card.fires_on: Punctuation or short words that open a news story's body or a quote: opening quote marks, the dash after a dateline, "Day" in "HealthDay News", and speech verbs like said or added.

modes.label: Dateline ends
modes.description: The last piece of a news dateline or byline right before the story text begins.
modes.example: MONDAY, July 18 (Health<<Day>> News) — Women fear Alzheimer's disease

modes.label: Quote openers
modes.description: An opening quotation mark that starts a quoted statement after a study claim.

modes.label: Attribution verbs
modes.description: A speech verb after a named researcher or authors, introducing what the study found.
modes.example: Dr Koplin<< said>> the study, published in journal Allergy

card.plain: It marks the spot in a health news story where the real text or a quote begins, or where someone is credited with saying something.
